recordings.caption: Striatal neuronal calcium: baseline field. Tavakoli et al. (2024).
recordings.directly_taught_event: Follow neuronal calcium events in the baseline striatal field before acute cocaine is applied.
recordings.original_preparation: Supplementary material 1 Raw unprocessed videos demonstrating astrocyte GCaMP6f fluorescence in slices from tdTomato (video 1) and hPMCA2w/b animals (video 2). Frame numbers are indicated in the upper left. Original videos were acquired at 25 Hz but are presented at 125 Hz for illustration. Arrows in the hPMCA2w/b video 2 highlight two astrocytes with brief periods of activity (e.g., left arrow: frames 950–970; right arrow: frames 1042–1087). Raw unprocessed videos demonstrating neuronal GCaMP6f fluorescence in slices from tdTomato and hPMCA2w/b animals are in videos 3-7. aCSF_M4 video 3 corresponds to the field of view in  Figure 4B . aCSF_M5 video 4 corresponds to the field of view in  Figure 5B ; cocaine_M5 video 5 is the same field of view after bath application of cocaine, corresponding to  Figure 5C . aCSF_M4 video 6 is the field of view in  Figure 6B ; NPS_F9 video 7 is the same field of view after bath application of NPS-2143, corresponding to  Figure 6C . Note that the onset of neuronal fluorescence is near instantaneous rather than spreading through the soma and syncytium territories as Ca 2+  “waves” characteristic of astrocyte signals. In cases where neuronal processes are captured in the imaging plane, fluorescence in neuronal processes always accompanies fluorescence in the soma they are connected to. This is not the case for astrocyte Ca 2+  where soma and process fluorescence can be independent of each other.
